cards.back: The study of disease, its causes, mechanisms, and effects on the body.
A protective response to injury or infection characterized by redness, swelling, heat, and pain.
Death of cells or tissues due to injury, disease, or lack of blood supply.
An increase in the number of cells in a tissue or organ.
An increase in the size of cells, leading to enlargement of an organ or tissue.
The transformation of one cell type into another, usually in response to chronic irritation.
Abnormal development or growth of cells, often a precancerous condition.
Programmed cell death, a normal process for removing damaged or unnecessary cells.
Insufficient blood supply to tissues, leading to oxygen and nutrient deprivation.
Death of tissue due to lack of blood supply, often caused by blocked arteries.
